title: Audio, speech recognition & synthesis
summary: From sampled waveforms to transcriptions, speech generation, and streaming systems.
html:
From sampled waveforms to transcriptions, speech generation, and streaming systems.

Represent sound digitally

A waveform samples amplitude over time. Sample rate controls temporal sampling; bit depth or floating-point representation controls amplitude resolution. Spectrograms organize energy across time and frequency. Resampling requires filtering to avoid aliasing. Channels and loudness are separate from semantic content.

Automatic speech recognition

ASR maps audio to text, often using learned acoustic representations and a sequence model. Word error rate counts substitutions, deletions, and insertions relative to a reference, but it does not capture every usability concern. Names, accents, background noise, and code-switching deserve separate evaluation.

Text-to-speech and voice

TTS converts text or phonemes into acoustic representations and waveforms; modern systems may generate audio tokens. Evaluate intelligibility, prosody, speaker consistency, pronunciation, and latency. A signal with normal loudness and no clipping can still sound unnatural. Voice permissions and provenance matter for deployment.

Streaming adds systems constraints

Chunk size affects first-response delay and context. Endpoint detection decides when a speaker has finished. Interruptions require canceling queued generation and playback. Echo cancellation, device buffering, and network jitter can dominate perceived performance even with a fast model.

Worked example

One minute of mono audio at 24,000 samples per second in 16-bit PCM uses 60×24,000×2 = 2,880,000 bytes before a container header. Compression changes storage size; it does not change the original sample count.

What goes wrong

Optimizing only word error rate can miss catastrophic errors in numbers or negation. TTS quality must include listening tests, not just waveform statistics.

Check your understanding

Why does smaller streaming chunk size not always improve the experience?

Reveal the explanation

It can reduce buffering delay while harming context, prosody, throughput, or network efficiency. Measure the whole interaction.

How the pieces connect

Capture → Represent → Model → Experience. Each transition is a place where an assumption can be inspected before the next layer of the system compounds it.

An operating model for audio, speech recognition & synthesis

Audio systems live at the intersection of signal processing and interaction design. A transcript can be statistically strong yet fail on names, numbers, accents, or turn boundaries. A synthesized voice can be intelligible yet unnatural, too slow, or unsafe for the intended identity and consent context.

The diagram is deliberately sequential, but real systems loop. A surprising result may expose a bad representation; a production incident may reveal a missing evaluation slice; a performance limit may require an algorithmic change. The point is to preserve the link between the abstract concept, the evidence you observe, and the decision you make next.

Worked system: the transcript that fails the call center

An ASR system may achieve an attractive average word-error rate while repeatedly missing account numbers, medication names, negations, or names spoken with an underrepresented accent. Those errors are sparse in the aggregate but decisive in the workflow. Streaming adds a second layer: an accurate transcript that begins too late, fails to recognize interruption, or talks over a user can still feel unusable.

Evaluate recordings from the actual microphones, rooms, languages, and network paths. Break down errors by the entities that matter, measure first-audio and final-transcript latency, and let humans listen to synthesized output. Audio is both a signal-processing problem and a turn-taking interaction.

Notebook: Budget the real-time loop

Use this as an inspection pattern, not a drop-in production implementation. The specific values will change, but the habit remains: expose the assumption, calculate the boundary, and preserve the evidence that supports the next decision.

frame_period_ms = 1000 / 30
perception_ms = 18
control_ms = 4
assert perception_ms + control_ms < frame_period_ms
# Leave a margin for transport, jitter, and recovery.
What to test next. 1. Capture: Sample sound with known devices, rate, and channels. 2. Represent: Transform waveform into features or audio tokens. 3. Model: Recognize, synthesize, separate, or classify sound. 4. Experience: Stream with interruption, timing, and human listening tests.

A rigorous way to practice

  1. Capture. Sample sound with known devices, rate, and channels.
  2. Represent. Transform waveform into features or audio tokens.
  3. Model. Recognize, synthesize, separate, or classify sound.
  4. Experience. Stream with interruption, timing, and human listening tests.

Evaluate recordings from the real microphones, rooms, languages, and noise conditions. Measure first-audio latency and interruption handling alongside recognition or synthesis quality.

Questions that keep the chapter honest

AskWhy it mattersEvidence to collect
What assumptions does this method make?Every method encodes a view of data, hardware, or behavior.Inputs, representations, constraints, and cases outside the expected range.
What would make the result fail?Failure modes show where an aggregate result is fragile.Boundary cases, counterexamples, slices, and perturbations.
What decision changes if it improves?A metric only matters through an operational action.Baseline, threshold, cost, latency, and human-review consequences.
